summary: Reinhold Klotz was a linguist who studied at Leipzig University from circa 1826 to 1829. He held a post at Leipzig University from circa 1832 to 1870 and taught Friedrich Max Müller.

Reinhold Rost worked in Indology and linguistics after studying at the University of Jena (~1843–1847). He served at The King's School Canterbury, St Augustine's College, the Royal Asiatic Society, and as Librarian of the India Office and India Office Library.

Renate Syed is an Indologist who studied at Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich from circa 1973 to 1982, earning her doctorate under supervisor Dieter Schlingloff and teachers Friedrich Wilhelm and Gritli von Mitterwallner.
Renda Zheng is a scholar in Buddhist studies who received instruction from traditional teachers Kaizhi, Shengfa, and Kaitong.

René Gothóni is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies who studied at the University of Helsinki from circa 1971 to 1977. He later held a post at Helsinki from circa 1979 to 2014 and taught Ilkka Pyysiäinen.

Richard A. Hutch is a religious studies scholar who studied at Gettysburg College, Yale Divinity School, and the University of Chicago. He held positions at Southern Illinois University (~1974–1978) and the University of Queensland (~1978–2010).
Richard B. Martin worked in Indology and Tibetology. He held posts at the University of Virginia, serving as Professor (attested 1983–1991) and South Asian bibliographer (attested 2003).
Richard Baker is a Buddhist studies figure who studied at Harvard University (~1954–1958) and under Shunryu Suzuki in 1971, whom he succeeded. He later taught Taigen Dan Leighton and Philip Whalen.
Richard Barron is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied under traditional teachers Kalu Rinpoche, Dezhung Rinpoche Kunga Tenpai Nyima, and the 3rd Jamgön Kongtrul.
Richard Bowring is a scholar of Japanology and Buddhist studies who was educated at Blundell's School (~1960–1965) and Downing College (~1965–1973).

Richard Carnac Temple, a scholar of Indology and history/archaeology, studied at Harrow School and Trinity Hall. He served in the Bengal and Indian Staff Corps and was proprietor and editor of The Indian Antiquary.
Richard D. Mann is a scholar in Indology and religious studies who earned his PhD at McMaster University under the doctoral supervision of Phyllis Granoff (attested 2003).

Richard D. McBride II, a scholar of Buddhist studies, sinology, and history/archaeology, studied at UCLA under mentor Robert E. Buswell Jr. He held a postdoctoral fellowship at Washington University in St. Louis and a post at Dongguk University.

Richard F. Nance works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and religious studies. He completed his PhD at the University of Chicago by 2004 and held a faculty post in religious studies at Indiana University (attested 2013).
Richard Fick was an Indologist who studied at the University of Kiel from circa 1885 to 1888 and later held a post at the University of Göttingen from circa 1921 to 1932.

Richard Foltz is an Iranian and Central Asian studies, religious studies, and history scholar. Educated at the University of Utah and Harvard, he held posts at the University of Florida (~1999–2006) and Concordia University, where he was Founding Director (~2006).
Richard Fritzsche was an Indologist who studied under Hermann Brockhaus from circa 1872 to 1877 and later served as Rektor at Gymnasium Schneeberg.

Richard Gombrich is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who earned his D.Phil. at Oxford under Robert Charles Zaehner. He served as Boden Professor of Sanskrit at Oxford and Balliol College and was General Editor for Clay Sanskrit Library.

Richard Hugh Robinson was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. Educated at Alberta, SOAS, and London, he held posts at the University of Toronto and the University of Wisconsin-Madison, where he served as Professor starting in 1961.

Richard Hughes Seager is a religious and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Wisconsin System, Harvard Divinity School, and Harvard University (PhD ~1982–1987). He was appointed Associate Professor of Religion at Hamilton College around 1994.
